close_reason: Analysis: hickory 0.26.0-alpha.1 wraps NXDomain in ProtoErrorKind::NoRecordsFound with response_code=NXDomain (error.rs line 614-636). The existing NoRecordsFound { .. } pattern already catches it. No code change needed.
description: mta_sts_dns.rs:28 only matches ProtoErrorKind::NoRecordsFound to return Ok(None) (no MTA-STS). But NXDomain (the subdomain _mta-sts.example.com does not exist at all) is a separate ProtoErrorKind variant. An NXDomain response falls through to Err(DnsLookupFailed), which in enforce_for_delivery logs a warning and allows delivery — but that is already the correct outcome. The real consequence is that the warning is noisy and misleading for every domain that simply has no _mta-sts subdomain. RFC 8461 §3.1 treats both NXDOMAIN and no STSv1 record as 'no policy'; the distinction matters for clean logging and correct semantics. Fix: match both NoRecordsFound and NxDomain (or its equivalent in hickory) to Ok(None).
title: NXDomain on _mta-sts lookup causes DnsLookupFailed instead of Ok(None)
